title: Audemars Piguet Royal Oak and Gérald Genta

slides.title: The steel watch that cost more than *gold.*
slides.body: In 1972, a steel watch priced like gold was unthinkable. Gérald Genta sketched one in a single night.

image.credit: Royal Oak ref. 15202, modern successor of the 1972 original · Photo: OpaleHorse · CC BY-SA 4.0

slides.title: Luxury meant *gold*
slides.body: A prestige watch was thin, elegant and made of precious metal. **Steel was for tool watches.** Then AP's agents asked for something new: a steel sports watch as elegant as gold.

slides.title: A phone call at *4 pm*
slides.body: On the eve of the Basel fair, AP's director calls designer Gérald Genta. He wants a revolutionary steel watch, **and he wants the design by the next morning.**

slides.title: Inspired by a *diving helmet*
slides.body: Genta remembered a diver on a Geneva bridge being fitted with a helmet: **eight bolts and a rubber seal.** By morning, the octagonal bezel was on paper.

image.credit: A Siebe Gorman diving helmet (for illustration) · Photo: Daderot · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

slides.title: Sketched overnight. *Built in two years.*
slides.body: The case was so new and complex that the first prototypes were made in white gold. **It took two years** to go from the sketch to the Basel fair.

slides.title: The most expensive *steel watch*
slides.body: At Basel, the Royal Oak costs **CHF 3,300**. In the same year's catalogue, one of AP's own yellow-gold watches costs CHF 2,990.

slides.title: Both, *in a way*
slides.body: AP sold 490 in 1972, an AP record for a single model. Yet until 1976 the Royal Oak stayed **under 7% of AP's production.**

slides.title: Genta's own *Royal Oak*
slides.body: His personal watch, a steel model with a unique gold bezel, sells at Sotheby's Geneva for **CHF 2,107,000**. Not bad for a design sketched in one night.

slides.title: Fifty years later, steel is the *new gold.*

caption:
In 1972, Audemars Piguet asked people to pay more for steel than for gold. 🔩

The Royal Oak was sketched by Gérald Genta in one night, inspired by a diving helmet, but it took two years to build and years more to win people over. Today it's one of the most famous watches ever designed.

Royal Oak or Nautilus? 👇

Sources: Audemars Piguet archive (AP Chronicles); Time+Tide; Monochrome; Quill & Pad.

review_notes: Independent fact-check (fact-checker subagent): PASS WITH FIXES → required fix and optional improvements applied. See factcheck.md.
Year of the call: AP says 1970, some press says 1971. We follow AP's dated archive.
Launch price varies by source (3,300 / 3,500 / 3,650). We use AP's figure; the gold-watch comparison has one source (Time+Tide citing AP's 1972 catalogue).
Avoided 'saved AP from the quartz crisis' and '10x a Submariner' (not supported).
No free photo of the 1972 ref. 5402 exists: the cover uses its modern successor, labelled as such. Genta's studio portrait was not used.
